clue.text: Remove head of fruit without speed, turning it

indicators.note: in its old sense 'without' means outside, so one piece wraps around the rest

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

indicators.note: something turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pace is rate of movement
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing fruit: cut off the top, then turn it slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the fruit wraps everything else. 'Remove head of fruit' reads as one instruction, but only 'Remove head' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decapitate is literally to cut off a person's head, from Latin caput meaning the top part of the body.

clue.text: Pack in part of ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pack of playing cards
second meaning: a floor level on a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone stows their gear in a section of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a verb about stowing luggage, but it is the noun: a full set of playing cards, which Americans and Britons alike also call by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of playing cards and a flat floor level aboard a vessel share this one word.

clue.text: Constant request for beer container

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A drinker keeps asking for a barrel of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: C for a constant is a science convention, from equations such as E = mc squared.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden barrel in which real ale is stored and served in British pubs.

clue.text: Fashionable until I can be seen filling in jobs for some artists

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something else, so these letters are placed within others

parts.note: posts are positions of employment
what is in is in fashion
till means until
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trendy people show up in roles for artists until they become fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' and 'jobs' both read as everyday description, but each stands for a short synonym; three pieces fill the jobs word, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointillists, such as Seurat, painted pictures from tiny dots of pure colour, a nineteenth-century French technique.

clue.text: First of all, tries wild and noisy guitar sound?

definitions.text: First of all, tries wild and noisy guitar sound?

indicators.note: the first of every one of the following words is taken, all of them

parts.words: tries wild and noisy guitar sound
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A guitarist tries playing wild, loud chords to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the initials spell the answer, and the clue read straight describes what a wild, noisy guitar does.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the sharp, ringing note of a plucked string, typical of country or surf guitar playing.

clue.text: Ditch final third of fodder in plate

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch

indicators.note: the closing third of a six-letter word is its last two letters

parts.note: the final two of its six letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrape the last of the animal feed off a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning throw away, but it is the noun TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is an old wooden board or platter on which food was served and cut.

clue.text: Terrific story shown in huge picture-house

indicators.note: what is shown in something is displayed inside it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A great film is playing at a huge cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A picture-house is an old word for a cinema, which makes the hidden answer sit naturally in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic tale, and the word as slang also praises something as terrific.

clue.text: Unevenness of feature aboard head ship

indicators.note: whatever is aboard is carried within a vessel, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the chin is a facial feature
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A complaint about a lopsided figurehead on a ship's prow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head ship' suggests a flagship, but it splits into two separate pieces: an old word for the skull, then the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchiness is the quality of being irregular, good in some places and poor in others.

clue.text: Fed up as dairy product, initially delicious, gets rancid

parts.note: cheese is made from milk

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter
food that has gone off is spoiled

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up because a delicious dairy product has turned rancid.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage food that has 'gone off' has spoiled, so OFF stands for rancid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is informal British slang for annoyed, bored or thoroughly exasperated.

clue.text: Players I confined to quarters and reprimanded

parts.note: the cast are the players in a production
taken as written
a student who is gated is kept within college as punishment

explanation.surface: A disciplinary story: players are grounded and told off.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is a British school and university punishment confining a student to the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to criticise or scold severely, a formal word for a harsh telling-off.

clue.text: Animal house reported infection

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: a sty is a pen where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: A farm building has been found to carry disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig pen and the eyelid swelling are pronounced identically but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small painful bacterial swelling on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: Place in the desert has its cake tally prepared

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready by working on it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A desert outpost has its baking count ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' could be any town, and the three-word enumeration points to a city name.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Utah lies beside the Great Salt Lake amid arid basin country of the American West.

clue.text: Actors' helpers, perhaps, in old-fashioned transport

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read whimsically: trainers who coach people for the theatre

definitions.note: a mass noun standing for the plural vehicles
definitions.meaning: second meaning: horse-drawn passenger vehicles running between towns

explanation.surface: Theatre assistants travel by horse and carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word into its parts: coaches who work with actors on the stage. 'Perhaps' flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn coaches carrying passengers and mail on fixed routes were the long-distance travel of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Decent butcher's uttered deliberate misinformation

indicators.note: what is uttered is spoken, so the sound of the words counts, not their spelling

parts.note: proper means decent or respectable
rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: A respectable butcher has been spreading lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look, so 'have a butcher's' means take a look, and a gander is also a look. 'Proper gander', said with a non-rhotic British accent, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased or false information spread deliberately to promote a political cause.

clue.text: He sells lots of gold once rite's arranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A merchant once sold a great deal of gold in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like 'a great quantity', but it means items for sale at an auction. The 's after rite is the contraction of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer conducts a public sale, offering numbered items to bidders and selling each to the highest offer.

clue.text: Difficulty skimming top off foreign currency

indicators.note: skimming removes the uppermost layer, so the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: trouble is difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble for skimming money off a foreign currency deal.
explanation.walkthrough: TROUBLE loses its T. In a down-or-across clue 'top' means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the monetary unit of Russia, divided into one hundred kopecks.

clue.text: Determined in advance Democrat needs it badly

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Democrat is fixed on winning because they need it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: D for Democrat is the US political label, as in a senator listed (D).
explanation.definitionFit: Something destined is fated beforehand, its outcome settled by fate or design.

clue.text: Top actor autograph: Leo perhaps

parts.note: a star is a leading performer
to autograph is to sign

explanation.surface: A fan collects a famous actor's signature; perhaps it is Leonardo DiCaprio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like an actor's first name, but 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve zodiac signs used in astrology and horoscopes.

clue.text: Loyalists knock disturbances in the street

parts.note: a pat is a light knock or tap
riots are violent public disorder

explanation.surface: Loyal supporters criticise unrest on the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like the verb to criticise, but it gives a gentle tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriots are people devoted to their country and faithful to its cause.

clue.text: Church service when in large, elevated area

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharist service
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: A religious service held when in a high, open place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as part of the setting, but it simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains or a raised block of the earth's crust.

clue.text: Dump person on mother? It's a mark of shame

parts.note: Stig of the Dump is a British children's novel about a caveboy living in a chalk pit
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Leaving someone with their mother is a disgraceful thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a verb meaning abandon, but it names the setting of Stig of the Dump, Clive King's 1963 children's book, well known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is social disgrace attached to a person or circumstance, originally a brand burned into skin.

clue.text: Winter G&T cocktail with shot: concocted by one person, but credited to another

definitions.text: concocted by one person, but credited to another

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the ampersand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender's winter gin-and-tonic with an extra shot was invented by one bartender but credited to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concocted' sounds like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'cocktail' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost-written book or speech is composed by a hidden writer and published under somebody else's name.

clue.text: One research facility put up in tropical island

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
short for laboratory

explanation.surface: A research station is built on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' reads as 'built', but in a down clue it sends I + LAB upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island near the equator, famous for beaches and Hindu temples.

clue.text: Give up plant ovule, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported has been said aloud, so pronunciation matters here

parts.note: a fertilised ovule becomes a seed

explanation.surface: A gardener abandons a plant's tiny reproductive part.
explanation.walkthrough: The botanical term pushes toward a plant word, but only its sound is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender territory, rights or ground to another party.

clue.text: Return of one chap or another associated with Xmas

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: the word itself is tied to Christmas

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Leon is a man's name

explanation.surface: One man or another comes back at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon reversed gives Noel, another man's name, hence 'or another'; that second chap is the one tied to Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for Christmas, seen in carols and on cards, and a name given to boys born then.

clue.text: Insolence about dismal period in devout journey

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk
grim means gloomy
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Rudeness during a gloomy time on a religious trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' or a container signal, but here it turns LIP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey to a shrine or holy site made for religious reasons.

clue.text: Deaf Roman sporting this hairstyle

indicators.note: to sport something is to wear or carry it, so the words hold the letters within them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Roman who cannot hear has an unexpected haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This hairstyle' points back at the word the Roman is wearing, so the definition only works once the answer is found.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, voluminous style of naturally tightly curled hair.

clue.text: Kind EU ally, confused and indelicate

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly European partner is muddled and tactless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as an adjective in the surface, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unladylike behaviour is coarse or improper by old standards of polite female conduct.
